equation_request.abstract: Although a universal quantum computer is still far from reach, the tremendous advances in controllable quantum devices, in particular with solid-state systems, make it possible to physically implement “quantum simulators”. Quantum simulators are physical setups able to simulate other quantum systems efficiently that are intractable on classical computers. Based on solid-state qubit systems with various types of nearest-neighbor interactions, we propose a complete set of algorithms for simulating pairing Hamiltonians. Fidelity of the target states corresponding to each algorithm is numerically studied. We also compare algorithms designed for different types of experimentally available Hamiltonians and analyze their complexity. Furthermore, we design a measurement scheme to extract energy spectra from the simulators. Our simulation algorithms might be feasible with state-of-the-art technology in solid-state quantum devices.

specification.problem: Simulate a pairing Hamiltonian (BCS/Richardson-type reduced pairing model) on a solid-state qubit array with nearest-neighbor interactions, and extract its energy spectrum by a measurement scheme. The abstract gives no explicit equations, so only a tiny background instance is reconstructed.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest construction: a 2-pair-level reduced pairing Hamiltonian mapped to 2 qubits (pair occupied/empty), Trotterized time evolution, and phase-estimation-style spectrum extraction by Fourier transform of a time signal. The paper's specific nearest-neighbor gate decompositions, fidelity studies, complexity comparisons across Hamiltonian types, and its actual measurement scheme remain outside scope.

symbols.meaning: single-particle level energy of pair level j
pair creation/annihilation operators on level j (hard-core boson, qubit raising/lowering)
Pauli raising/lowering and Z operators on qubit j

equations.label: Pairing Hamiltonian
equations.latex: H=\sum_{j}2\epsilon_j\, b_j^\dagger b_j - G\sum_{j,k} b_j^\dagger b_k
equations.description: Standard reduced pairing (BCS-type) Hamiltonian in pair operators; level energy is doubled for pairs.
equations.justification: Generic form of a pairing Hamiltonian; the abstract names pairing Hamiltonians but gives no form.
assumptions: Reduced BCS form with uniform coupling G
Not claimed to be the paper's exact Hamiltonian

equations.label: Qubit mapping
equations.description: Hard-core pair occupation encoded as one qubit per level; |0> empty, |1> occupied.
equations.justification: Proposed encoding for the tiny instance.
assumptions: Qubit j corresponds to level j, ordering q_0 then q_1

equations.label: Two-qubit instance
equations.description: Two-level instance: diagonal terms (number terms with j=k) plus an XY exchange term hopping a pair between levels, which is a nearest-neighbor XY-type interaction.
equations.justification: Direct substitution of eq_2 into eq_1 for 2 levels, using \sigma^+_0\sigma^-_1+h.c.=(XX+YY)/2.
assumptions: The vanishing-coefficient term is a placeholder that equals zero and carries no content

equations.label: Trotterized evolution
equations.description: First-order Trotter approximation (approximate, not exact) with error O(t^2/n).
equations.justification: Standard method for simulating Hamiltonians with gates.
assumptions: H_m are the diagonal Z terms and the XX+YY term

equations.label: Spectrum from time signal
equations.description: Time-domain signal whose Fourier transform peaks at eigenvalues E_k.
equations.justification: Common route to energy spectra; the paper's actual scheme is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Re and Im of S(t) estimated via an ancilla-controlled evolution or Ramsey-type measurement

registers.name: q
registers.role: system qubits encoding pair occupation of levels 0 and 1

registers.name: a
registers.role: ancilla for Hadamard-test estimation of S(t)

specification.initial_state: |\psi_0\rangle=|01\rangle (one pair in level 1), ancilla in |+\rangle; assumed choice

steps.description: Prepare the system in the reference state and the ancilla in |+>.
Apply the controlled Trotterized evolution for time t using the mapped Hamiltonian.
Measure the ancilla in X and Y bases to estimate Re and Im of S(t) at multiple times.

specification.measurement: Ancilla measured in X and Y bases for a grid of times t.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Discrete Fourier transform of S(t) over sampled times; peak positions give eigenvalues E_k up to resolution ~2\pi/T_max.
assumptions: No scope was given; the 2-level instance with Hadamard-test spectroscopy was chosen
Hamiltonian form and measurement scheme are generic background, not the paper's
Fidelity analysis, hardware-specific nearest-neighbor decompositions and complexity comparison not reconstructed
